missionPremise: P-230 asks a discriminator question, not a fix: between (a) 'the bake is scheduled and simply has not run for these parcels, so the gap is latency' and (b) 'nothing re-bakes a parcel when its cells change, so the gap is structural', and the row forbids assuming (a) because it is cheaper. The premise the row rests on -- quoted from its own card -- is 'Cells are written, the gate sees them, and the customer surface serves a bake from before the write', fired on two independent rows (P-200: get_smart_site on the Hays gold parcel returned not-cut-over with an identical runId and bakedAt after the setback apply; P-211: after a 107,544-cell envelope apply, 48209:100226 still read maxHeightFtFact refused with a bakedAt predating the apply). The dispatch's grounding read (readBakedNodeFacetSnapshot -> SELECT ... FROM place_layer_snapshots WHERE adapter_key IN (tier1,tier2) AND place_key='node:{fips}:{propId}') is confirmed by this lane: the customer's baseFacts are a materialized table, and the only question is whether and how it refreshes.
completionPredicate: Stated so a stranger can evaluate it: (1) the bake's trigger mechanism is named by reading the code, or its absence is named with the resource enumeration that proves absence; (2) a written cell reaches get_smart_site for a named parcel with a bakedAt LATER than the write, cited from a live customer read rather than from a gate verdict; (3) the affected population is bounded -- the six ledger counties or the 19-county bake-only set. THIS LANE CLOSES (1) IN FULL AND (3) IN FULL, AND CANNOT CLOSE (2): no trigger exists to fire, AND the customer facets read is refusing project-wide today on an unrelated credential mismatch, so no lane could close (2) this session. (2) stays open and is the row's remaining predicate.
scopeBasis: legacy-design-tools (the bake CLI's own repo) plus read-only reads of hauska-factory (where the bake's only caller lives) and of three live stores; NOT lib/cad-ingest/src/boundary/ and NOT lib/db/src/schema/, because P-241 held a live claim on both throughout this lane and this row has no reason to touch either. No new county, no product-surface change, no schema change, no deploy: every one of those is either another row's scope or an operator stop point. The lane deliberately did NOT execute the bake to test hypothesis (a), because (i) a write to a production serving store is one of only three operator stop points, (ii) the trigger read already decides the question without a 194,538-row county rewrite, and (iii) executing a Job that nothing schedules and then noting it worked would have proved the wrong thing -- that a human can bake, which was never in doubt.
falsifier: FIRED, all four, in the direction the row said not to assume. F1 (read the trigger): the bake has NO trigger -- not a cron, not a job schedule, not a queue consumer, not even an expected manual step. The only writer of place_layer_snapshots for the node path is nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts (plus its tier2/pmtiles siblings and one backfill script); it is reachable only through hauska-factory (invokeLdtBake in src/jobs/bastrop-publish.mjs:190, dispatched at src/cli.mjs:137, deployed as Cloud Run job factory-bastrop-publish at cloudbuild.publish.yaml:389), and `gcloud scheduler jobs list` returns exactly TWO jobs in the entire project (us-east4; us-east1/us-central1/us-west1 empty): factory-conformant-reap (*/10) and factory-publish-gate-sched-hourly (0 * * * *). Neither executes the bake, and publish-gate-sched.mjs writes parcel_gate_verdict only -- read in full to prove it, not inferred from its name. F2 (reproduce (a) or (b) live): (b). On 48209:100226 and 48209:97658, NINE cells each were written to the production ledger AFTER the served bakedAt (5 setback* at 2026-09-15T00:55:31.535Z, 4 envelope at 2026-09-15T16:34:27.618Z for 100226; 16:34:51.542Z for 97658), by two runs that both report status succeeded (38026b23 / parcel-setback-cells / 2026-09-15T00:54:13Z and ca4d022f / parcel-envelope-cells / 2026-09-15T16:32:51Z). In the 25.8 hours since, publish_runs gained ZERO rows, while the project's other automations ran 176 times (f03-reap 152 success, publish-gate-sched 24 succeeded). The control makes it causal rather than coincidental: 48209:34137, which the same September work did not touch after its bake (last cell write 2026-09-13T23:52:32Z, before its bakedAt of 2026-09-14T17:35:53Z), is the one of the three that is NOT stale. F3 (fresh write end to end): NOT PERFORMED AS A WRITE, and the dispatch's own alternative branch CONFIRMED -- it never refreshes without manual intervention. I did not write a cell (production serving store = operator stop point 2; publish-gate-sched.mjs itself refuses --apply off Cloud Run under LAPTOP_WRITE_FROZEN), and I did not fire the bake, for the reasons in scopeBasis. What replaces the timing is stronger than a timing: two real succeeded writes, twenty-five hours, zero bakes. F4 (scope): the SIX LEDGER COUNTIES, not the 19 -- parcel_record holds exactly six county prefixes (48021, 48055, 48209, 48309, 48453, 48491) while place_layer_snapshots serves 19, so the other 13 have no cells for anything to enqueue and their newest bake is 2026-07-22..2026-08-05 (A-184's population, not this row's). Inside that: FIVE of the six are stamped 2026-09-10 in freshness -- six days stale by publish alone, before the cell-write gap is even considered.
contradicted: ONE LOAD-BEARING PREMISE OF THE CARDING DOES NOT SURVIVE, and it is the premise the fix would have been built on. The row's framing implies a chain in which a cell write is an input the bake reads, so that the open question is only whether something enqueues a re-bake. Half of that chain is missing. nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts:3 states its input: 'F-06 Tier-1 facet bake from conformant-v1 hauska_mcp atoms', and its read is `SELECT entity_id, body FROM atoms WHERE ...` (line 354) against ATOMS_DATABASE_URL -- the bake reads the ATOMS store, not the ledger. And the writers that touched these parcels mint no atom: parcel-envelope-cells.mjs writes parcel_record_cell only (UPDATE parcel_record_cell prc at line 205; its own header names 'a hand UPDATE/INSERT on parcel_record_cell' as the sole other writer) and parcel-setback-cells.mjs is the same shape. Therefore, for the envelope and setback rails, a cell write is not by itself an input the bake can see, and a trigger that enqueued the parcel would re-materialize the same atoms and produce the same payload. The dispatch's proposed fix class ('a cell write must enqueue its parcel') is thereby NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT as written, and the honest restatement is that place_layer_snapshots is a second, hand-refreshed copy of what the 2026-09-11 ruling already declares the serving path for these rails. Separately contradicted: the row's completion predicate cannot be measured by anyone today -- https://smartsite.cloud/api/spine/property-atoms/{id}/facets returns HTTP 503 retrieval_auth_failed ('HAUSKA_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY must match retrieval-api RETRIEVAL_API_KEY') for every parcel tested (48021:34049, 48209:97658, 48209:100226, 48453:474034), so the customer's facets read refuses before it reaches any bake; the probe corroborates it (all five P-175 facets legs read `http 503 readPath null bakedAt null`). NOT contradicted, and worth saying because the row invited the finding: this does bear on closes graded on a gate verdict, but not as an error in those closes -- a gate verdict answers 'is this rail gradeable from the ledger' and the customer's baseFacts come from the baked table, so a green gate and a stale customer answer were never measuring the same store. A close that cited a gate verdict as evidence the customer sees a value was grading something the customer may not see; a close that cited a surface-probe artifact was not.
leave_behind: THE TRIGGER IS ABSENT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE ROW. Nothing runs the bake. The only entry point is `gcloud run jobs execute factory-bastrop-publish --project=hauska-prod-497015 --region=us-east4 --wait --args=bastrop-publish,--target=production,--county=<fips>` run by a person (hauska-factory/src/jobs/bastrop-publish.mjs:190 invokeLdtBake; :28-35 documents the invocation as a hand command; cloudbuild.publish.yaml:389 defines the job with staging/Bastrop defaults). Any fix must create a caller; there is nothing to repair.

FIX CLASS: (b) structural, not 'a faster schedule'. The dispatch's own trap applies with a measured number now: one publish rewrites the WHOLE county -- Hays tier1Written 194,538 rows, Travis 873,766, Williamson 602,050 -- so a schedule tick that catches up nothing still rewrites everything. A faster schedule narrows the window and pays that cost per tick without ever closing the gap that a single unchanged parcel cannot pull itself forward.

THE NEXT SEAT'S MOST USEFUL MEASUREMENT, WHICH THIS LANE COULD NOT MAKE: does an atom exist for these rails on 48209:100226? The bake reads the atoms store, and parcel-envelope-cells.mjs/parcel-setback-cells.mjs mint no atom, so the answer decides between two different fixes: if atoms exist, the fix is a per-parcel enqueue into the bake (or nothing at all, if the intent is to serve these rails from the ledger); if they do not, no trigger can help these rails and the answer is the 2026-09-11 ruling's own law -- THE LEDGER IS THE SERVING PATH -- with place_layer_snapshots retired or rebuilt as a cache of it. A per-parcel atoms lookup by entity_id TIMES OUT (~120 s statement timeout) with no usable index; the next seat needs the indexed access path before anything else. Corresponding probe leg for P-254: 'served bakedAt >= the parcel's latest parcel_record_cell.updated_at', which today would FAIL by construction on every Hays parcel touched on 2026-09-15 -- exactly what a predicate should do.

FIVE OF THE SIX LEDGER COUNTIES ARE SIX DAYS STALE BY PUBLISH ALONE. freshness.stamped_at: production:48209 = 2026-09-14T17:51:01.975Z, and production:48021 / 48055 / 48309 / 48453 / 48491 = 2026-09-10. That is a second, independent staleness -- no cell write required -- and it means Phase 0's 'the six onboarded counties complete and verified' has no cadence behind it for five of the six.

LIVE PROJECT-WIDE CUSTOMER-SURFACE REFUSAL, 2026-09-16T18:1xZ, NOT P-230 AND NOT ABSORBED: every /api/spine/property-atoms/{id}/facets call returns HTTP 503 retrieval_auth_failed -- 'HAUSKA_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY must match retrieval-api RETRIEVAL_API_KEY'. Tested on four parcels in three counties (48021:34049, 48209:97658, 48209:100226, 48453:474034) and corroborated by the probe's five Hays facets legs. The customer's fact path is refusing; card it to whoever owns retrieval-api's key wiring before any close cites a facets read.

COST TELEMETRY IS STILL ABSENT, AND THIS ROW WOULD NEED IT. Any per-parcel enqueue scheme is a metered cost question, and publish_runs carries only body jsonb plus created_at/completed_at -- the same hole law 5 names. Named so the fix is not designed against an unmeasurable cost.

REUSABLE ENVIRONMENT GROUND-TRUTH FOR THE NEXT SEAT (this cost this lane two abandoned probe runs): node in this session cannot complete TLS without --use-system-ca (set NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca). Without it every outbound fetch fails as 'fetch failed' and surface-probe.mjs writes an all-UNMEASURED artifact ('fetch failed' on every network leg) that looks like an honest measurement of a dark surface. NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=P:/tmp/corp-ca-bundle.pem alone is NOT sufficient ('unable to verify the first certificate'). PowerShell's Invoke-WebRequest does work and exposes a JSON error body via $_.ErrorDetails.Message (the response stream reader returns empty).

TWO SCHEDULED-RUN FAILURES IN THE WINDOW, NAMED BECAUSE NOBODY ELSE HAS: publish-gate-sched failed once at 2026-09-15T20:01:53Z (24 succeeded around it) and f03-reap crashed once at 2026-09-16T15:00:16Z (152 succeeded). Neither is P-230 and neither was investigated by this lane. The hourly gate is the only control watching cell quality in six counties, and one of its ticks failed silently to anyone not reading the runs table.

PROCESS, HONESTLY: the doc_repo commit gates (fan-depth, probe-close) do not fire in a seat worktree until P-280 lands, so subAgents.spawned=0 and the probe citation are honest declarations, not enforced ones. The lane claim for p230-bake-trigger was held by this seat throughout and is released at close; a claim by seat dispatch-planner for p241-etj-acquisition was live in the same repo throughout, which is why the boundary/schema paths were never touched.
processDisclosure: FAN-DEPTH 0 was honoured literally: no sub-agent was launched, and every line of evidence above was produced by this session (subAgents.spawned 0, maxDepth 0). The lane was claimed first via scripts/lane-claim.mjs (exit 0, live from 2026-09-16T18:02:51.797Z) and is released at close. One process note against myself: the probe artifacts were produced twice, and the FIRST run (_inbox/2026-09-16_181530_surface_probe.json) is all-UNMEASURED with 'fetch failed' on every network leg -- a node TLS failure in this environment, not a dark surface. It was nearly filed as a measurement of a refusing customer surface, which would have been the exact defect this program's law 1 exists to catch. The second run, after NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca, is the only artifact cited. A second self-criticism: the atoms-store question that decides the fix class (does an atom exist for maxHeightFt on 48209:100226) was approached by LIKE '%48209:100226%' on a table large enough that the server cancelled the statement, and then by exact entity_id with the same timeout. Both attempts were heavy scans on a store under a one-scan-at-a-time rule; the right move was to read the atom lookup's schema and index first, and the lane spent its atoms budget on two queries that returned nothing. The measurement is left open and named, rather than papered over with an inference from the writer's source.
honestPartialStatement: This close says closed-partial because the row's completion predicate has three legs and this lane closes two. Leg 1 (name the mechanism, or its absence, with a file citation) is CLOSED: the bake has no trigger, cited to hauska-factory/src/jobs/bastrop-publish.mjs:190 and cloudbuild.publish.yaml:389, with the absence proved by enumerating every scheduling resource in the project. Leg 3 (bound the population) is CLOSED: the six ledger counties, not the 19. Leg 2 -- a written cell demonstrably reaching get_smart_site with a bakedAt later than the write -- is NOT closed and CANNOT be closed by any lane today, for two independent reasons: there is no trigger to fire, and the customer facets read is returning 503 on a credential mismatch unrelated to this row. Adding the finding that the bake reads atoms while these cell writers mint none: the row's proposed fix ('a cell write must enqueue its parcel') is not sufficient as written, and the next seat should settle the atom question before building it.
